sources.title: Retained six transparent 9.18 hand derivations, independently reinspected
sources.details:
Original hand derivations2026-10-30T09:59:04.193995+00:00; immutable path docs/technical-reviews/artifacts/omni-P5-9.18/hand-derivations-v1.json SHA434d50a7bee4d3538b17273bd3b35f338993ae49bcbcf52eb095a36e2762961c. Current owner re-read d1–d6 after receipt, preserving their scope. d1: For finite logits and T>0, z_i/T > z_j/T iff z_i>z_j. exp is strictly increasing and each same-question denominator is common, so class ranking, ties and argmax are preserved in real arithmetic. Across two different questions, denominators differ; this does not preserve p_max order. At T=1: X=1/(1+2*exp(-1)), Y=1/(1+exp(-0.5)+exp(-10.5)); 2*exp(-1)>exp(-0.5)+exp(-10.5), hence X<Y. At T=0.1: X=1/(1+2*exp(-10)), Y=1/(1+exp(-5)+exp(-105)); 2*exp(-10)<exp(-5)+exp(-105), hence X>Y. The recorded rounded pairs are (0.57612,0.62245) and (0.99991,0.99331); no class winner changes.
d2: Set a=3^(1/T), q=a/(a+2). The three probabilities are (q,(1-q)/2,(1-q)/2). The five labels have counts (3,1,1). L(q)=-(3*ln(q)+2*ln((1-q)/2))/5. dL/dq=-3/(5q)+2/(5*(1-q)); dL/dq=0 implies q=3/5. d2L/dq2=3/(5*q^2)+2/(5*(1-q)^2)>0, so this is the unique minimum for q in (0,1). q=3/5 implies a=3 and T=1, present at k=16 in the 33-point grid 0.25*2^(k/8), k=0..32. Grid endpoints are 0.25 and 4. At T=1, probabilities are exactly (3/5,1/5,1/5). Mean NLL=-(3*ln(3/5)+2*ln(1/5))/5, rounded to 0.9503. This is a Choice-only artificial five-family objective, not the actual three-type objective.
d3: At T=1, maxima for top logits 4,3,2 in the given patterns are 1/(1+exp(-4)+exp(-6)), 1/(1+exp(-3)+exp(-5)), 1/(1+exp(-2)+exp(-4)). They lie respectively between .975 and .99, between .9 and .95, and between .85 and .9. Policy rows 1,2,3 are correct accepts at tau=.9. Row4 is a high-card wrong answer below .9, row5 predicts none, and row6 predicts information=no. At tau<=.85 the first four are accepted and one is wrong: 4/6 coverage, 1/4 risk. At .9:3/6 and0/3. At .95 or .975:2/6 and0/2. At .99:0/6 and risk undefined. Among positive-accept grid settings with empirical risk<=.05, .9 uniquely maximizes coverage. Risk0 is observed sample performance, not a guarantee.
d4: Original wording accepts first two: n=2,e=0,N=3,coverage2/3,risk0. New wording accepts first and third: first chooses wrong gold, third falsely says sufficient; n=2,e=2,N=3,coverage2/3,risk1. Combined final has N=6,n=4,e=2:coverage2/3,risk1/2. At tau=1 no row is accepted and risk is None. none/handoff remain in N. Exercise changes only the third new-wording info prediction toFalse, with T/tau unchanged. New wording:n=1,e=1,N=3,coverage1/3,risk1. Combined:n=3,e=1,N=6,coverage1/2,risk1/3. No gold field enters the take decision. Unsupported/sufficiency/choice gold flags enter only the retrospective Boolean error OR, so errors count per accepted question and overlapping causes count once.
d5: 39/60=0.65. Positive T preserves the 39 winners; changing probability scores does not improve top1 correctness. 53/60=0.883333..., reported88.3%. 19/53=0.358490566..., reported35.8%. Choice accuracy denominator60 differs from accepted-risk denominator53. If n independent target-family successes were observed with zero errors, any true failure probability r in (0,1) still assigns positive probability (1-r)^n to that event. Thus a finite zero-error sample cannot imply zero population risk. Sibling variants are dependent, so family grouping is needed. Fitting L_cal(T) gives no deterministic inequality for L_final(T): they sum different gold-labelled rows. The saved final NLL increase is an explicit project example, not evidence that calibration always harms.
d6: If an interface returns s=z/T0, then s*T0=z. Softmax is also invariant to adding a constant to every class score, so centered logits can be restored up to an irrelevant common offset. This rule does not invert arbitrary probabilities or unknown score transforms. For instance z=(1,0,-1),T0=.5 yields s=(2,0,-2), and multiplying s by .5 restores z. The synthetic code averages five Choice losses equally. Formal saved calibration has80 families, each with Choice/info/rubric; the objective averages three types within each family, then80 family means. Repeated variants do not increase the independent-family count.
